correctness.rationale: For W_n=K_1 vee C_n, n>=5, each C4 consists of the hub and three consecutive rim vertices and is contained in exactly the corresponding five-edge diamond; the extra spoke is already distinct from the other spokes by properness, making B- and D-constraint systems identical. With n hub-spoke colors normalized to i, each rim edge e_i excludes spoke labels i-1,i,i+1,i+2; therefore c(e_i)=i+d_i with d_i in {3,...,n-2}. The only remaining conflicts are adjacent rim edges, equivalent to d_i != d_(i+1)+1 as integer reps. The constant offset 3 gives an n-color solution, matching hub degree. Transfer matrix T_(u,v)=1 unless u=v+1 counts cyclic offset words as tr(T_(n-4)^n); global color-name action is free. At n=3 W3=K4 has all 6 edges pairwise conflicting; n=4 rim C4 adds B rainbow restriction requiring 8 rather than D=6 alternating, one color orbit each. Independent transfer count confirmed n5..8 counts 1,2,367,11966; direct exceptional structures follow from proof and source verifier.
